jobs.description:
A Non-Medical Care Manager contributes to AHF by Providing coordination, guidance, and assistance in improving access to and retention of needed medical support to mitigate and eliminate barriers to HIV care services. With a caring and knowledgeable focus, you will work with our providers and healthcare center team so that every Ryan White client receives the support they require and access to available resources. Completing Initial Assessments and developing Individualized Care Plans related to psychosocial needs and goals. You will draw on your experience and skills in understanding basic needs such as housing, food, and clothing, develop relationships with programs and agencies serving those needs, and facilitate referrals and support groups, and assistance for your clients who lack those services. In this way, you will support the client’s ability to better understand their health status so that they can work to achieve their healthcare goals. You will also conduct ongoing retention calls to ensure no gap in retention efforts and to uphold radical cooperation across divisions.

A Non-Medical Care Manager enhances the reputation of AHF by utilizing your case management experience, you will meet our clients where they are, identify strengths and opportunities for growth, and assist them with realistic goal setting. With your skills of collaboration and engagement, you will bring the essence of the Ryan White Care Act - the safety net for uninsured HIV/AIDS patients- to our most vulnerable population. Your needs assessments, care plans, referrals, and support will directly contribute to WORLD/AHF’s success in meeting the deliverables of our Ryan White contract. Beyond the scope of the contract, your work contributes to measures established by the HIV/AIDS Bureau (HAB) Measures and the Department of Health and Human Services. You will verify the client’s eligibility for the ACA (Affordable Care Act) program and enroll those who qualify to ensure broader access to healthcare services.

You will be a passionate advocate for our top initiatives.

To be successful as a Non-Medical Care Manager it is crucial to ensure that the AHF Core Values and Mission stay top of mind with all that you do. At AHF we are nimble and able to adapt in a dynamic environment to assist in providing the best experience for our clients and workplace for our employees.

AHF has a collaborative organizational structure where staff are accountable to multiple leaders.

The Non-Medical Care Manager will work as a part of a close-knit team to collaborate with the provider and client to implement the optimum care plan for these non-medical needs by improving access to care and retention. Advocate on behalf of clients to decrease service gaps and remove barriers to service. Work with the client for better health and social service outcomes and quality of life. Licenses and Certifications: Bachelor degree in health or human services-related field preferred.

A minimum of 1 year Case Management experience is preferred. Knowledge of Ryan White Services is preferable.

Our Company

Overview

StepStone Family & Youth Services provides trauma informed, youth centered services to children and families involved in foster care. The Foster Care Case Manager plays a vital role in supporting youth and foster families through therapeutic case management, service coordination, and individualized support that promotes safety, stability, permanency, and positive outcomes.

We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Foster Care Case Manager who is passionate about supporting children and families through trauma informed, strengths based, and family centered practices. This role is ideal for a professional who understands the impact of trauma, loss, and disrupted family systems and is committed to helping youth and families build resilience and long term success.

The Foster Care Case Manager works closely with foster families, biological families, treatment teams, schools, and community providers to support placement stability, emotional wellbeing, and coordinated care for youth in foster care placements. Through ongoing communication, advocacy, and service planning, this position helps ensure youth and families receive responsive and supportive services tailored to their unique needs.

The ideal candidate is organized, adaptable, empathetic, and committed to delivering high quality services while maintaining professionalism, compliance, and a trauma informed approach throughout all aspects of service delivery.

Responsibilities

The Foster Care Case Manager works under the supervision of the Program Manager. They are responsible for the delivery of case management services, individual and family counseling and training and supervision of foster families. The Foster Care Case Manager assists the Program Manager in developing individual treatment plans for troubled children and their families. They maintain weekly contact with the foster families, children, and bio-families and monitors the progress of the child and family throughout the placement. They assist with training, home studies, and evaluation of foster parents. The Foster Care Case Manager uses standardized tools to measure social and emotional progress and outcomes and prepares written treatment plans and progress reports.

PERSONAL WORK RELATIONSHIP: The Foster Care Case Manager makes decisions regarding the placement and treatment of neglected, abused, disturbed, and medically complex children. He or she will have good verbal and writing skills. They will be capable of working with children, parents, foster parents, client agencies and the courts. The Foster Care Case Manager will be creative, pragmatic, assertive, and know when to act independently and when to seek the advice of others.

EXAMPLES OF DUTIES. The position includes, but is not limited to, the following:

Reviews referrals and matches children with appropriate foster families.
Places children in state licensed or state certified foster homes.
Obtains all state and agency required documentation for child in care.
Provides weekly documented contact and at bi-weekly visits to child and foster home.
Visits each assigned child at least once each month away from the foster home.
Prepares a treatment plan for the child within 21 days of placement and quarterly thereafter.
Prepares monthly progress reports for assigned children.
Provides Independent Living training and monthly ILP progress reports for assigned clients.
Provides reunification services to the biological families when required by treatment plan.
Coordinates visitation of children with biological parents, siblings, and relatives.
Provides supervised visits with parents, siblings, and relative when required by court.
Acts as liaison person with placing agencies, schools, and other community agencies.
Attends court hearings and review hearings.
Attends staff meetings and treatment planning meetings as required.
Completes interviews, training and home studies on prospective foster parents as needed.
Attends conferences and seminars as required for annual training requirement.
Conducts/participates in two or more foster parent support group meetings each year.
Maintains flexible working hours and works weekends or holidays as needed.

Qualifications

The Foster Care Case Manager has a bachelor’s degree in social work, sociology, psychology, counseling, or related human services field and two years’ experience working with children and families. A bachelor’s degree in social work, sociology, psychology, counseling, or related human services field and five years’ experience with a placing agency working with troubled children and families may be consider in lieu of a graduate degree.

About Our Line Of Business

StepStone Family and Youth Services, an affiliate of BrightSpring Health Services, provides the full spectrum of support to children in need of alternative, safer, and more positive living environments with residential and family services. StepStone connects children and youth who need homes with foster families, as well as foster care training, respite care and support services. For young adults transitioning from foster care to independent living, StepStone provides personalized guidance and training on basic life skills, including money management and education. For more information, please visit www.stepstoneyouth.com . Follow us on Facebook and LinkedIn .

About the Brian Grant Foundation

The Brian Grant Foundation (BGF) empowers people impacted by Parkinson’s to lead active and fulfilling lives.  We do so by being open about our struggles and by sharing our wins. We serve the whole person, supporting mind, body, and spirit. We embrace evidence-based and practical ways to improve daily living. And we remember to laugh and have fun, creating connections and defying stereotypes about living with PD. Together, we create what truly sets the Brian Grant Foundation apart: community. We’re here for one another, and we’re here to make life better.

Position Overview

The  Program Manager
 leads the day-to-day planning, operational implementation, coordination, and data-informed evaluation of BGF’s portfolio of wellness and community support programs. Working in close partnership with the Executive Director, the Program Manager translates strategic priorities into accessible, engaging, and participant-centered experiences—both online and in-person.

This role requires an organized, tech-savvy, and collaborative leader with strong organization and interpersonal skills. The Program Manager is often in situations where they will represent the Brian Grant Foundation and must be a strong spokesperson and comfortable in multiple social contexts. An understanding of and commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging is a core competency. 

The Program Manager will often collaborate cross-functionally across the organization. This includes working with the: 

Communications Manager to develop outreach strategy and program messaging.
Development Director to translate program metrics, outcomes, and participant impact into clear, compelling narratives for grants, funders, and sponsors.
Executive Director to design and implement long-term programmatic strategy.
Subject matter experts who BGF contracts with to deliver programs.

Key Responsibilities

Program Strategy, Operations & Delivery
Program Oversight & Delivery:
 Oversee the end-to-end planning, logistics, scheduling, and delivery of virtual and in-person programs.
Strategic Alignment:
 Partner closely with the Executive Director and the Program Advisory Council to refine existing offerings and launch new evidence-based program initiatives.
Technical & AV Execution:
 Set up, test, troubleshoot, and operate audiovisual (AV) equipment, live-streaming software, and hybrid meeting technologies to ensure seamless virtual and in-person participant experiences.
Budget Management:
 Develop and manage annual program budgets in coordination with leadership; monitor program-related expenditures and evaluate budget performance on a quarterly basis.

Data Collection, Management & Continuous Improvement
Data Infrastructure:
 Lead the collection, organization, and ongoing management of program data across all virtual and in-person touchpoints (attendance, engagement metrics, surveys).
Data-Informed Decision Making:
 In partnership with the Executive Director, establish benchmarks, analyze program trends, and regularly synthesize and evaluate data to assess program effectiveness.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
Outreach & Messaging Strategy:
 Partner with the Communications Manager to establish outreach calendars, provide accurate program details, define audience segmentation, and align messaging to boost community participation.
Grant & Funder Alignment:
 Collaborate with the Development Director to ensure program deliverables align with grant commitments, sponsorship agreements, and reporting timelines. Be a key programmatic spokesperson, ensuring team members and BGF constituents understand programs and know how to describe their impact. 
Community & Stakeholder Relations:
 Represent BGF at relevant regional outreach events and conferences in coordination with the Executive Director. Cultivate strong relationships with those who engage with the foundation. 

Team Leadership & Program Facilitator
Instructor & Facilitator Coordination:
 In partnership with the Community Liaison and other stakeholders, recruit, onboard, schedule, and support expert wellness instructors, guest speakers, and facilitators across all programs.
Volunteer Oversight:
 Oversee program volunteers and advisory working groups, providing clear expectations, training, and ongoing support.

Qualifications & Competencies

Required Qualifications

Education & Experience: 
Bachelor’s degree preferred; plus 3–5 years of experience in program coordination, project management, or community wellness programming. A master's degree may substitute for additional years of work experience. 

Technical Proficiency & AV Skills:
Proficiency in operating and troubleshooting AV equipment, live-stream platforms, microphones, and hybrid event setups.
Proficiency across the Microsoft 365 suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, SharePoint).

AI Fluency: Practical skill in leveraging generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot) to elevate operational efficiency, data synthesis, and workflow planning, balanced with sound judgment to  avoid relying on AI to generate primary strategic deliverables.

Data & Analytical Skills: Proven ability to collect, organize, analyze, and present data and survey metrics to drive continuous improvement.

Communication & Interpersonal Tact: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills across diverse audiences (people living with Parkinson’s, care partners, medical professionals, donors, and volunteers) with proven presentation and facilitation skills.

Organizational Excellence: High attention to detail, strong time-management skills, and the capacity to juggle multiple deadlines and deliverables independently.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with Salesforce (or similar non-profit CRM database).
Lived or professional experience working with neurodegenerative conditions, chronic health populations, older adults, or caregiver support networks.
Familiarity with virtual programming models, cohort-based learning, wellness coaching, or nutrition and exercise.

Working Conditions & Physical Demands

Work Arrangement:
 Hybrid role based in the Portland, OR metropolitan area, combining remote flexibility with regular in-person presence for local events, workshops, and team meetings. Regular schedule is Mon- Fri, 8:30 AM to 5 PM, with occasional weekend and evening commitments. Some travel outside the Portland metro area, to include Oregon or Washington, may be required.   

Schedule:
 Occasional evenings or weekends required to support specific program sessions, meet-ups, or community outreach events.

Physical Requirements:
 Ability to transport, lift, and set up AV and event supplies up to 25 lbs per item.

Salary Range:
 $65,000 to $72,000 dependent on experience. Includes flexible work schedule, PTO, Health and Dental Benefits, Retirement Plan, Holidays off and potential for a performance- based bonus.

Overview

LMI is seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead the delivery of LMI's technology portfolio supporting the United States Postal Service (USPS). USPS operates the nation's largest delivery and logistics network and is in the midst of a multi-year modernization effort to improve service reliability, transform the customer experience, and achieve long-term financial sustainability. The TPM will be LMI's senior technical leader on this account: owning the end-to-end deployment of technology solutions into the USPS environment and serving as the trusted advisor who connects hands-on engineering execution to USPS mission and business outcomes.

This is a hands-on leadership role for a professional who can lead the deployment of a diverse portfolio of enterprise technologies into a large, complex federal environment, including ServiceNow, the Microsoft ecosystem (Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Azure), AI-enabled and agentic solutions, custom software applications, AI-assisted software engineering approaches, and commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) products. The TPM manages a portfolio of concurrent technology projects and deployments, sets and enforces best practices across software development, customer/user experience (CX/UX) design, security, and release management, and is personally accountable for the cost, schedule, quality, and adoption of every solution the team delivers. Equally important to the technical mandate is customer management and relationship building. The TPM builds and sustains strong working relationships with USPS stakeholders, translating their needs into actionable solution roadmaps, communicating clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences, driving consensus, and continuously demonstrating value. The role demands someone who thrives in an environment that emphasizes building, deploying, and iterating in parallel, and who can own the full solution lifecycle alongside the client.

Role Scope & Authority

This senior leadership role reports to the LMI USPS Account Lead and serves as LMI’s primary technical leader on the account. The position oversees a portfolio of multiple concurrent technology initiatives and leads a multidisciplinary team of engineers, architects, designers, analysts, and subcontractors.

The TPM has broad authority to set delivery standards, prioritize and sequence work, approve technical approaches, escalate risks to USPS and LMI leadership, and recommend staffing and resource decisions. The role interacts regularly with USPS senior IT and business stakeholders at the director and executive levels.

About LMI

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Portfolio Delivery & Execution:
Serve as LMI's senior technical lead and primary technical point of contact for the USPS account.
On-time, on-budget delivery of technology solutions into the USPS production environment across multiple platforms and technologies.
Build and sustain trusted relationships with USPS stakeholders, acting as the senior advisor on solution approach and continuously identifying opportunities to add value and expand impact.
Own the end-to-end lifecycle of technology deployments into the USPS environment (e.g., intake, solution design, build, integration, test, deployment, and sustainment)
Prioritize, sequence, balance workload, and allocate resources to effectively manage and deconflict a portfolio of concurrent technology projects and deployments

Translate USPS mission and business needs into technical solution architectures, delivery roadmaps, and Agile backlogs that integrate cleanly with existing USPS systems, data, and enterprise IT.
Lead delivery using Agile methodologies (Scrum, SAFe, and/or Kanban): manage the backlog, sprints, and release planning; run ceremonies; and drive CI/CD and DevSecOps practices for fast, reliable, and secure delivery.
Apply human-centered design and CX/UX best practices throughout delivery so solutions are usable, accessible, and adopted, not just deployed.

About Making Opportunity Count

Making Opportunity Count’s mission is to empower families to achieve economic security by eliminating barriers and creating opportunities. To alleviate poverty, we deliver a variety of services including childcare, education, workforce development, nutrition, health, and community and housing support.

Position Overview

The Shelter Case Manager is responsible for providing comprehensive case management services to families residing in shelter. Using motivational interviewing and strength-based practices, the Case Manager works collaboratively with participants to develop individualized rehousing plans that include clear goals, measurable action steps, and targeted interventions designed to promote self-sufficiency and secure safe, stable, and affordable permanent housing.

Shelter Case Managers are cross-trained in the Stabilization Program and may be assigned to provide Stabilization services as needed to support program operations and ensure continuity of client services.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Establish reoccurring monthly rehousing meetings with families.
Provide accurate written notices of meetings according to EOHLC Uniform Shelter Rules, Scope of Services, and program requirements.
Review and address barriers to housing (credit score, criminal record, history of nonpayment, setting up bank account).
Collect required vital records, financial documents, legal documents, and other necessary records to complete and maintain participant files. Supports participants with retrieving needed documents if necessary.
Review client preferences and needs for tenancy (location, roommate(s), etc.).
Create a budget to ensure housing sustainability (what can client afford vs. wants and needs).
Document case management efforts and services through clear, detailed, and thorough case notes in ETO for each family to include weekly meetings, client, and collaborative contacts, as well as any significant events and/or interactions within 24 hours of meeting.
Provide education about affordable housing options. Works collaboratively with other department staff.
Make referrals for support and services participants may need.
Updates weekly meeting reports, housing placements reports, and any other reports as required. Determine need and advocate for reasonable accommodations when needed.
Reports and updates of any program rule violations, missed meetings or concerns to appropriate leadership personnel to process noncompliance requests. Consistently meets all EOHLC Scope of Services and agency contract outcome goals with respect to housing efforts, housing placements, rehousing plans, and data collection.
Participate in all required training and professional development activities. Performs other duties as assigned.
Conduct home visits for participants receiving Stabilization services to assess housing stability, monitor progress toward goals, provide supportive case management, and connect families with community resources
Maintain accurate and timely documentation of all home visits and participant interactions in accordance with program and agency standards

Problem-solving abilities.

Position Overview

The Shelter Case Manager is responsible for providing comprehensive case management services to families residing in shelter. Using motivational interviewing and strength-based practices, the Case Manager works collaboratively with participants to develop individualized rehousing plans that include clear goals, measurable action steps, and targeted interventions designed to promote self-sufficiency and secure safe, stable, and affordable permanent housing.

Shelter Case Managers are cross-trained in the Stabilization Program and may be assigned to provide Stabilization services as needed to support program operations and ensure continuity of client services.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Establish reoccurring monthly rehousing meetings with families.
Provide accurate written notices of meetings according to EOHLC Uniform Shelter Rules, Scope of Services, and program requirements.
Review and address barriers to housing (credit score, criminal record, history of nonpayment, setting up bank account).
Collect required vital records, financial documents, legal documents, and other necessary records to complete and maintain participant files. Supports participants with retrieving needed documents if necessary.
Review client preferences and needs for tenancy (location, roommate(s), etc.).
Create a budget to ensure housing sustainability (what can client afford vs. wants and needs).
Document case management efforts and services through clear, detailed, and thorough case notes in ETO for each family to include weekly meetings, client, and collaborative contacts, as well as any significant events and/or interactions within 24 hours of meeting.
Provide education about affordable housing options. Works collaboratively with other department staff.
Make referrals for support and services participants may need.

Reports and updates of any program rule violations, missed meetings or concerns to appropriate leadership personnel to process noncompliance requests. Participate in all required training and professional development activities. Performs other duties as assigned.

Maintain accurate and timely documentation of all home visits and participant interactions in accordance with program and agency standards
